evidence.location: section 2 RP1, lines 163-164 ('A join that GND would refuse as disconnected is refused by name, before lowering.') and criterion RP1-C6 (line 240)
evidence.observation: The plan's only named-join-refusal rule is the disconnected case, and RP1-C6 tests only that. But GND's join admission has a second refusal the plan never mentions: _require_joinable raises JoinAmbiguousError when a single referenced fact type has more than one non-referenced (anchor) role of the same object type — src/gnd/checker/_core.py:1182-1184 reads 'if len(role_names) > 1: raise JoinAmbiguousError(fact_type_id, object_type_id, role_names)'. The RP1 draft spec's binding scheme (phase-RP1-spec.md lines 80-83: 'Each non-referenced role binds $<object type>_1 in copy one and $<object type>_2 in copy two') maps both ambiguous roles to the SAME variable, silently equating two distinct roles. The DuckDB program would then render and enforce a join that gnd check refuses to compute, violating the plan's own binding rule in section 0 ('Same verdict as GND. A program reports a rule as not checked exactly where gnd check does', lines 52-54) for any such model. No planned test (RP1-C3/C6, spec T4/T9/T12/T13) constructs this case. The plan's claim that the lowering reproduces the checker's join 'exactly as _join_rows merges anchors' (lines 157-160) is therefore incomplete.

concerns.recommendation: Extend RP1 (plan section 2 and criterion RP1-C6, and the RP1 spec's connectivity step) to also refuse, by name, a referenced fact type carrying two non-referenced roles of the same anchor object type, mirroring JoinAmbiguousError in _require_joinable (_core.py:1182-1184), and add one default-lane test fixture for it.
concerns.title: RP1 join admission omits GND's JoinAmbiguousError, so the program can enforce a join GND refuses
